title: $30 an Hour Buys a Robot Housekeeper in San Francisco
snippet: Tau Robotics began sending humanoid robots into San Francisco homes in late July for $30-an-hour cleaning visits. Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley engineering professor with 40 years in the field, expressed skepticism about the technology's readiness, stating, 'I really think it is too early.'

title: From Documentation to Zero-day Vulnerabilities: LLM-Driven Fuzzing of JavaScript Engines in PDF Readers
snippet: Existing fuzzers for PDF readers rely on simple test cases that involve only individual API calls, leading to limited coverage and potentially missing vulnerabilities. To address these limitations, we propose PDFuzzer, a novel PDF engine fuzzer that automatically generates complex and meaningful API call sequences using a Large Language Model (LLM).
match_reason: websearch (publication) — Giovanni Vigna is a co-author of this paper, which applies Large Language Models (LLMs) to cybersecurity fuzzing.
